definition: Emotional dependence is emotional reliance on an AI system that can develop as part of a user’s emotional interaction with it. In this context, it is treated as a distinct feature of AI emotional engagement.

reasons: The packet does not define “emotional dependence”; it only mentions it as an example of “unique features of AI interactions” (with parasocial relationships) that existing studies have not targeted. Therefore, the definition’s claims about what it is (“emotional reliance on an AI system”) and how it “can develop” are not supported by the packet.
The packet does not support the specific framing that it is a “distinct feature of AI emotional engagement,” beyond a general statement that targeted measures are needed to capture unique features.
The packet provides background and instrument-development aims, but it does not provide enough content to justify the definition’s substantive assertions or the requested sense of the term.

The definition adds unsupported content by characterizing emotional dependence as “emotional reliance on an AI system” and as something that “can develop” through user interaction; the packet only says it is a unique feature of AI interactions.
The packet supports emotional dependence as a feature relevant to AI emotional engagement, but not the fuller causal/process description given here.
